title: AI-generated props or asset store packs: which is faster for a small team?
author: MogoHans
selftext: A small team choosing between generated props and asset store packs often faces a trade off between speed and fit, and the right answer may depend on what the game needs most. A store pack may offer polished models with clean topology and ready textures, though the style may not match the game and the pack may carry pieces the team never uses. Generated props may match a brief more closely, though each one may need cleanup, retopology and texture work before it behaves well in an engine. Time can be the deciding factor. A pack may be usable on the day it is bought, while a generated set may need days of checking and fixing before it is ready to place, so the total time may be closer than the first price suggests. Consistency can also matter. A pack with one style may read as a coherent world, while a generated set may drift unless a style reference and a triangle budget keep it steady. Tripo Studio is described as a browser based option with text to 3D and image to 3D and export in STL, GLB, FBX and OBJ, which may suit a starting draft to compare against a pack. Generation is only a starting point, since retopology, mesh repair, part splitting, texturing, slicing and print testing may still be needed. Before commercial use, verify rights to reference images, characters, logos and third party materials. For your team, what has saved more time, a pack or a generated set?
